paragraphs.title: The Warning and the Weeping at Bochim

answers: An angel of the Lord
Joshua
One of the elders
easy.explanation: The passage says, “And an angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim.”
easy.q: Who came up from Gilgal to Bochim?

answers: Built cities for them
Brought them out of Egypt and into the land
Appointed judges for them
easy.explanation: The angel said that the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt and into the land promised to their fathers.
easy.q: What did the angel remind Israel that the Lord had done for them?

answers: They went out to battle
They remained silent
They lifted up their voice and wept
easy.explanation: The people “lifted up their voice, and wept.”
easy.q: How did the people respond to the angel’s words?

answers: They had not obeyed the Lord or destroyed the altars of the inhabitants
They had not sacrificed at Bochim
They had not buried Joshua
medium.explanation: Israel had made no league as commanded and had not thrown down the inhabitants’ altars.
medium.q: Why did the angel rebuke Israel?

answers: They would become rulers over Israel
They would be as thorns, and their gods would be a snare
They would help Israel worship the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord said they would be “as thorns in your sides,” and their gods would be a snare.
medium.q: What would happen because the inhabitants remained in the land?

answers: A trap or source of entanglement
A place of residence
A sign of victory
medium.explanation: A snare is a trap or something that catches and entangles a person.
medium.q: What does the word “snare” mean in “their gods shall be a snare unto you”?

answers: The covenant was canceled because Israel wept
The Lord remembered His covenant while rebuking Israel for breaking it
The covenant was given only to the inhabitants of the land
challenge.explanation: The Lord said He would not break His covenant, while Israel had not obeyed His voice.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the covenant and the angel’s rebuke?

answers: Weeping alone did not bring real change
The people immediately stopped serving other gods
The people destroyed every altar
challenge.explanation: Although the people wept and sacrificed, the later verses show that their response did not produce lasting change.
challenge.q: What does the difference between the people’s weeping and their actions suggest?

answers: Because Joshua was buried there
Because the people wept there
Because a battle was fought there
challenge.explanation: The place was called Bochim after the people lifted up their voice and wept.
challenge.q: Why was the place called Bochim?

paragraphs.title: Joshua’s Death and the Forgetfulness of the New Generation

answers: To Egypt
Every man unto his inheritance
To Bochim
easy.explanation: They went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.
easy.q: Where did the children of Israel go after Joshua let them go?

answers: Only during Joshua’s lifetime
During Joshua’s lifetime and the lifetimes of the elders after him
Only after Joshua died
easy.explanation: The people served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived him.
easy.q: How long did Israel serve the Lord according to these verses?

answers: Joshua the son of Nun
The angel of the Lord
All the inhabitants of the land
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joshua the son of Nun died.
easy.q: Who died at the beginning of the transition to the new generation?

answers: It had not witnessed the works the Lord had done for the previous generation
Joshua had never entered the land
The elders served other gods
medium.explanation: A new generation arose after the death of those who had seen the Lord’s great works.
medium.q: Why did the new generation not know the Lord and His works?

answers: They had seen the great works of the Lord
They led Israel in serving Baal
They did not live beyond Joshua
medium.explanation: The elders outlived Joshua and had seen the great works that the Lord did for Israel.
medium.q: What was significant about the elders?

answers: They went to their inheritances
They died
They returned from Egypt
medium.explanation: In this context, being gathered unto their fathers refers to dying.
medium.q: What does the phrase “gathered unto their fathers” mean here?

answers: The death of Joshua and the elders, followed by a generation that did not know them
The weeping at Bochim
The nations remaining in the land alone
challenge.explanation: After the generation that had seen the Lord’s works died, another generation arose that did not know Him or His works.
challenge.q: What gradually led to the loss of knowledge of the Lord’s works?

answers: The former generation served the Lord, but the new generation did not know Him
Joshua is contrasted with the angel of the Lord
Egypt is contrasted with Gilgal
challenge.explanation: The earlier generation served the Lord, while the new generation did not know the Lord or His works.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 7–10?

answers: It explains why they served the Lord
It proves that they conquered all the land
It explains why they served Baal
challenge.explanation: The passage connects their witness of the Lord’s works with their continued service to Him.
challenge.q: Why is it important that the elders had seen the Lord’s works?

paragraphs.title: Sin, Punishment, and the Rise of the Judges

answers: Baalim and Ashtaroth
Joshua and the elders
The angel of the Lord
easy.explanation: The passage says that Israel served Baalim, Baal, and Ashtaroth.
easy.q: Whom did the children of Israel serve after forsaking the Lord?

answers: He delivered them into the hands of spoilers and enemies
He brought them out of Egypt
He sent them to their inheritances
easy.explanation: The Lord delivered Israel into the hands of spoilers and sold them into the hands of their enemies.
easy.q: What did the Lord do when Israel sinned?

answers: The elders
The judges raised up by the Lord
The inhabitants of the land
easy.explanation: The Lord raised up judges who delivered Israel from the spoilers.
easy.q: Who delivered Israel from those who spoiled them?

answers: Sin, punishment, the raising of a judge and deliverance, followed by sin after the judge’s death
Deliverance, sin, Joshua’s death, and the conquest of the land
A judge’s death, service to the Lord, return to Egypt, and deliverance
medium.explanation: Israel sinned, suffered oppression, was delivered through a judge, and returned to evil after the judge died.
medium.q: What recurring sequence appears in these verses?

answers: He repented because of their groanings and oppression
Israel had never served other gods
The enemies wanted to help Israel
medium.explanation: The Lord was moved by their groanings because of those who oppressed and vexed them.
medium.q: Why did the Lord deliver Israel in the days of the judge?

answers: Cries or sighs caused by distress
Inherited land
A covenant
medium.explanation: Groanings are cries or sighs expressing suffering and distress.
medium.q: What does “groanings” mean in this context?

answers: They went after other gods and bowed down unto them
The judges could not deliver them
Joshua sent them back to their inheritances
challenge.explanation: They would not listen because they went a whoring after other gods and worshiped them.
challenge.q: Why would the people not hearken even to the judges?

answers: The people remained faithful after the judge died
The judge was central to Israel’s deliverance during his lifetime
The judge ruled Israel before Joshua
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the Lord’s deliverance with His presence with the judge during the judge’s lifetime.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the statement that deliverance lasted “all the days of the judge”?

answers: Their change was not stable or inward
They no longer suffered from enemies
The judge led them to serve other gods
challenge.explanation: After the judge died, the people returned to corrupt ways, showing that their change had not lasted.
challenge.q: What does Israel’s return to evil after the judge’s death show?

paragraphs.title: The Nations Left Behind as a Test

answers: They had transgressed His covenant and had not hearkened to His voice
They had served the Lord
They had gone to their inheritances
easy.explanation: The Lord said Israel had transgressed His covenant and had not listened to His voice.
easy.q: Why was the anger of the Lord hot against Israel?

answers: Drive out any of the nations Joshua had left
Raise up any more judges
Hear the groanings of Israel
easy.explanation: The Lord said He would not henceforth drive out the nations Joshua left when he died.
easy.q: What did the Lord decide He would no longer do?

answers: To prove or test Israel
To offer sacrifices to the Lord
To send Israel back to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord left them to prove whether Israel would keep His way.
easy.q: Why were the nations left in the land?

answers: Israel’s disobedience led the Lord not to drive out the nations
Breaking the covenant caused the nations to serve the Lord
Breaking the covenant brought Joshua back to life
medium.explanation: Because Israel had not hearkened to the Lord, He did not continue driving out the nations.
medium.q: What was the connection between breaking the covenant and the nations remaining?

answers: To see whether they would keep the way of the Lord as their fathers had
To see whether they would conquer Egypt
To see whether they would build altars for the inhabitants
medium.explanation: The Lord tested whether Israel would walk in His way as their fathers had done.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the test placed before Israel?

answers: To remove or force out of the land
To give an inheritance
To appoint as a judge
medium.explanation: In this context, to drive out means to remove the nations from the land.
medium.q: What does “drive out” mean in this passage?

answers: The nations remained after Joshua’s death as part of the test
Joshua did not know the land
The nations already served the Lord
challenge.explanation: The Lord left the nations in the land after Joshua’s death in order to prove Israel.
challenge.q: Why does the passage say that the Lord did not deliver the nations into Joshua’s hand?

answers: The punishment was not driving them out, and the purpose was to test Israel’s obedience
The punishment was serving Baal, and the purpose was to raise up judges
The punishment was Joshua’s death, and the purpose was to return Israel to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The nations remained because of Israel’s covenant violation, and their presence tested whether Israel would keep the Lord’s way.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the punishment and the purpose of leaving the nations?

answers: The nations were not removed from the land quickly
The nations were immediately delivered into Joshua’s hand
Israel immediately left its inheritance
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord did not remove the nations quickly.
challenge.q: What does “without driving them out hastily” mean?
